title: Who This Door Is For
one_liner: Who this door is for: democratic socialists, building their own package in their own language.
scope_in: The audience — always addressed as democratic socialists, never as socialists; that this is not a general-audience site; why a neutral visitor goes to the .io instead.
scope_out: The mechanics of any plank below; anything addressed to the R, D or L audiences.

title: Replacing Incumbents Controlled by Special Interests and Money in Politics
one_liner: The core action: elect challengers to replace incumbents who answer to special interests and concentrated money instead of to the people who elected them.
scope_in: The voting record as the trigger; challengers who cannot be corrupted preferred over incumbents serving foreign interests; Citizens United as the specific fight this system is built to end.
scope_out: Naming individual people we cannot substantiate — we name the category, not the person.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Who exactly are you trying to replace, and how?

title: Meritocracy on This Community's Own Basis
one_liner: The engine underneath everything, run on the basis this community chooses for itself: the candidates most dedicated to citizens and strongest at refusing to be co-opted.
scope_in: Dedication measured after election rather than promised before it; the strength to refuse capture once in office; matching candidates to where a voter sits on the spectrum; open data, open source and open AI as the transparency that makes the claim checkable.
scope_out: The trust-score arithmetic itself, which is its own area.
newcomer_question_it_answers: How do you decide who is 'best' without just picking favorites?

title: Removing the Rigged Economy
one_liner: The Democratic Socialist community's own package for removing the rigged layer and getting back to an ethical, clean economy.
scope_in: A goal shared by all four doors but written here by democratic socialists in their own language; the package built by community voting; an economy ideal for workers as the headline rather than a footnote.
scope_out: The other three doors' versions of the same package.

title: Community-Based Voting and Collaboration
one_liner: The mechanism the whole platform runs on: positions, plans and candidate judgments come from citizens voting and working together.
scope_in: The community builds the package rather than receiving it; voting on where you sit on the political spectrum; how that keeps a loud minority from being mistaken for the whole.
scope_out: The platform-wide reasoning engine, which lives in the main app.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Who decides what this community stands for?

title: The Yearly Strategic Conference
one_liner: A yearly strategic conference for this community, where its direction gets set together.
scope_in: A .com-level event that each party door runs its own version of.
scope_out: Describing it as a movement-wide non-partisan event.

title: Economics That Work for Workers
one_liner: Economics is the center of this door, and every plank gets the same test: does it work for the worker.
scope_in: Wages, hours, healthcare, housing, childcare and debt — the ordinary economics of a working life; measuring candidates on whether their record actually moved those numbers.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What does this do for my paycheck?

title: An Economy Ideal for Workers in the Era of AI
one_liner: AI is changing what work is, and this community wants an answer before the disruption lands rather than after.
scope_in: Who captures the gains from automation — the citizen base or the same concentrated money that rigged the last economy; productivity gains reaching the people doing the work.
scope_out: Promising an outcome we cannot deliver.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What happens to my job when AI arrives?

title: New Colonialism: Foreign Interests Controlling US Politicians
one_liner: A new layer of colonialism gets added every year when foreign money buys influence over US politicians and US citizens pay for it.
scope_in: The mechanism — funding, lobbying, placed media, captured staff — documented with sources; challengers who will legislate the layers away; foreign leverage on an officeholder as disqualifying.
scope_out: Claims about a named person we cannot source.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Who is my representative actually working for?

title: Abortion Rights, and Why the Swamp Never Codifies Them
one_liner: The votes arrive and the promised codification never happens — because incumbents need the issue unresolved more than they need it fixed.
scope_in: Codification rather than re-litigation every cycle; the same swamp that keeps the economy rigged; money in politics as the mechanism underneath both.
scope_out: Measuring a candidate on whether they campaign on it rather than whether they will pass it.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Why has this never actually been fixed?

title: What Stays Up at the Non-Partisan Site
one_liner: Some things deliberately do not move down to this door, and this page points at the .io instead of quietly duplicating them.
scope_in: The neutral lobby and its single high-level plan; no religion up there and none on this door either; the read-only cross-party trust-score roll-up.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What is the difference between this site and the .io?

title: How This Door Relates to the Other Three
one_liner: Four party doors, one app: R Republicans, D Democrats, L Libertarians, S Democratic Socialists — four independent editions with no pairing between them.
scope_in: WeCitizensSocialism.com as edition S recognized by hostname; the other three doors and who each is for; why this door answers to marketing/messaging/socialism.md alone; the .io sending a visitor to the door they care about.
scope_out: Any attack on the voters behind another door — their captured incumbents are fair game, they are not. Any claim that one door mirrors or constrains another.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Is this a Democratic Socialist-only movement?

title: Our Board of Directors
one_liner: A real governance body that sits at the .com level, described accurately and never overstated.
scope_in: Why partisan governance belongs with the partisan community; the split between the .io's single high-level plan and the many partisan plans under this board.
scope_out: A board on the non-partisan side — there is none.

title: Partisan Laws and Bills
one_liner: Partisan law work happens on the .com doors, and this is where democratic socialists add and prioritize the laws they care about.
scope_in: Adding the laws this community cares about; the specific standing bills it cares about most; measuring a candidate against a concrete bill rather than a general statement.
scope_out: Law work on the .io — the non-partisan site does not host it.

title: Trust Scores
one_liner: Trust scores are how a citizen judges whether a candidate really works for citizens — built and voted here, at the party level.
scope_in: Democratic socialists building and voting the scores for their own candidates; what the scoring reflects; the read-only roll-up that appears on the non-partisan site.
scope_out: Voting on the .io — the roll-up there is read-only and nobody votes on it.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Where do I cast a vote that counts on a candidate?

title: Words We Use and Words We Avoid
one_liner: Language is the whole job of this door: two audiences never share a page, and we never claim a status we do not hold.
scope_in: The phrases that belong here — democratic socialists, working people, special interests, money in politics, Citizens United, new colonialism, the rigged economy; the phrases that never appear — socialists as a bare label, TPUSA replacement, the political right, Christian values, the non-partisan voice.
scope_out: Copy written for the .io or for the R, D or L audiences.
newcomer_question_it_answers: How should I talk about this?
